source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The question I selected

The opening came from the independent algebra attack, drawing on Astra’s N1137 approach to exact counting and uniform generation.

A chain complex consists of matrices

\[
R^{n_L}\xrightarrow{d_L}R^{n_{L-1}}
\longrightarrow\cdots
\xrightarrow{d_2}R^{n_1}\xrightarrow{d_1}R^{n_0}
\]

satisfying all the coupled equations

\[
d_i d_{i+1}=0.
\]

These matrices encode boundaries and homology. The compatibility condition is global: choosing or correcting one matrix affects the constraints on its neighbours.

I asked:

> **Can we construct exact generative coordinates for every such tuple over a finite local ring, retaining the multiplicities needed for uniform sampling, and determine the entire dependence on arithmetic depth?**

The selected ring class is **finite commutative chain rings**: rings whose ideals form one chain, with maximal ideal generated by a uniformizer \(\pi\). Two examples are

\[
\mathbb F_q[t]/(t^e)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb Z/p^e\mathbb Z.
\]

The first has polynomial coefficients and truncation; the second has integer carries. They can have the same residue field and length while having different arithmetic.

The construction resolves this question for all finite commutative chain rings with explicit arithmetic interfaces.

| Operation | Established result |
|---|---|
| Count | Exact number of all actual matrix tuples satisfying every adjacent-product constraint |
| Generate | Exact uniform sampling of those tuples |
| Convert | Deterministic, reversible conversion between ring families with the same identified residue field and length |
| Evaluate all depths | A finite integer transfer matrix and explicit rational generating function |
| Determine growth | Exact exponential rate, polynomial correction and positive leading constants |
| Describe typical deep reductions | Explicit limiting path weights, geometric residence counts and a Dirichlet law |

The objects counted are **actual matrices in fixed coordinates**. Changes of basis are used internally, with their multiplicities retained.

source_excerpts.text:
## 4. A stronger consequence: actual conversion between ring arithmetics

Equality of counts alone would leave the conversion problem untouched. The same coordinates give a **deterministic bijection between the actual complex sets**, preserving the entire residue differential.

The algorithm fixes one basis-selection rule depending only on the residue tuple. It then:

- extracts the gauge coordinates and minimal homology problem in the source ring;
- recursively transfers the smaller problem;
- retains the free digit and gauge coordinates;
- reconstructs using the target ring’s arithmetic;
- reverses the common residue basis change.

The reverse procedure recovers the original matrices exactly.

**This conversion uses no count table or enumeration of rank profiles.** Under the explicit arithmetic model, it has polynomial cost even when the number of grades varies.

A small example exposes why an actual construction is needed. Over \(\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z\),

\[
d_1=(1\ \ 1),
\qquad
d_2=\begin{pmatrix}1\\3\end{pmatrix}
\]

satisfy \(d_1d_2=0\).

Replacing binary digits by polynomial coefficients entrywise sends \(3\) to \(1+t\), giving

\[
(1\ \ 1)
\begin{pmatrix}1\\1+t\end{pmatrix}
=t\ne0
\]

over \(\mathbb F_2[t]/(t^2)\).

The implemented conversion instead returns

\[
\widetilde d_1=(1\ \ 1+t),
\qquad
\widetilde d_2=
\begin{pmatrix}1\\1+t\end{pmatrix},
\]

whose product is zero. Its inverse returns exactly the original integer-ring pair.

This is a reversible equivalence of finite ensembles. No additive, multiplicative, functorial or arbitrary homology-module correspondence is inferred from it. Its inputs are fully specified classical matrices, and reading and writing their entries is part of the cost.

## 5. One finite matrix determines every depth

The next step removes the need to treat each depth as a separate counting problem.

Let \(\mathcal H(\mathbf n)\) be the finite set of homology-dimension vectors reachable by residue-rank reduction. This set is closed under further reductions: two successive feasible rank profiles compose by addition.

Fix the root dimensions \(\mathbf n\). On these states, define the nonnegative integer matrix

\[
M_{\mathbf v,\mathbf h}
=
F_q(\mathbf v;\mathbf r(\mathbf v,\mathbf h))\,
q^{2b(\mathbf n,\mathbf v)+b(\mathbf v,\mathbf h)+E_1(\mathbf h)}
\]

for feasible reductions, with zero entries otherwise. Order states by decreasing total dimension, making \(M\) triangular. Set

\[
a_{\mathbf v}
=q^{b(\mathbf n,\mathbf v)}C_1(\mathbf v;q).
\]

Then

\[
\boxed{
C_{2m}(\mathbf n;q)=(M^m\mathbf1)_{\mathbf n},
\qquad
C_{2m+1}(\mathbf n;q)=(M^m\mathbf a)_{\mathbf n}.
}
\]

The matrix is independent of ring depth.

Consequently, the complete generating function is

\[
\boxed{
\sum_{e\ge0}C_e(\mathbf n;q)z^e
=
\left[(I-z^2M)^{-1}(\mathbf1+z\mathbf a)\right]_{\mathbf n}.
}
\]

It is an explicit rational function, computable by triangular substitution.

### A complete worked law

For dimensions

\[
\mathbf n=(2,3,2),\qquad q=2,
\]

the result simplifies to

\[
Z(z)
=
\frac{1-8z+1024z^2}
{(1-64z)(1-256z)^2}.
\]

Equivalently, at **every** depth,

\[
\boxed{
C_e
=
\frac{64^e}{8}
+
\frac{21e+14}{16}\,256^e.
}
\]

Thus the counts over both \(\mathbb Z/2^e\mathbb Z\) and \(\mathbb F_2[t]/(t^e)\) begin:

| Depth \(e\) | Exact number of complexes |
|---:|---:|
| 1 | 568 |
| 2 | 229,888 |
| 3 | 80,773,120 |
| 4 | 26,308,771,840 |

These values are consequences of the proved formula; the formula was not inferred by fitting them.

Rationality of congruence-counting series has classical general antecedents, including the work discussed by Denef, with credit there to Igusa and Meuser. The result here supplies this family’s explicit positive transfer matrix, sampler, ring-uniform arithmetic construction and growth law. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}
